header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Javier Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Anna Liu (Head of ML, Celestis), Mark Reyes (Platform Eng, Celestis), Sana Patel (CTO, Celestis)
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline for an open-model POC. Discussed shortlist (Llama-3/equiv, Mistral, MPT, Falcon variants), quality tradeoffs, multilingual/biomed needs, infra constraints (VPC/on-prem possibilities), and next steps to run benchmarks and share pricing. Action items assigned and target dates set.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (latency, p99, cost/token, quality)
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Javier: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making the time. Quick intro, I'm Javier, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya: Hi all.
[00:10] Anna: Hi, Anna here. Thanks.
[00:12] Mark: Mark in.
[00:13] Sana: Hi team.
[00:15] Javier: Cool, agenda is short: align on what success looks like for the POC, the workloads you want to test, share a shortlist of open models we think are a good fit, and then bench plan and timeline. Is that right, Anna?
[00:27] Anna: Yep that works. We want to validate accuracy on clinical note summarization and a multi-lingual triage classifier — Spanish and German mainly — and also check latency for synchronous API usage. Cost is important but accuracy is the primary metric.
[00:42] Priya: Great. Can you quantify accuracy? For summarization is there an eval set or human-grade labels?
[00:48] Anna: We have a small labeled set of about 500 gold summaries and then a larger unlabelled corpus. For the classifier, we have about 2k labeled examples across en/es/de. The docs are de-identified.
[00:59] Javier: Perfect, that's enough to get started. Mark, any infra constraints — VPC or on-prem?
[01:05] Mark: We prefer VPC private deployment, we need traffic to stay inside our network for the POC. We can do a short window for hosted but prefer private. Also need to check KMS integration for key management.
[01:17] Priya: Noted. Redwood Private supports VPC + bring-your-key via KMS, and we can run in your cloud region. There's a small setup window but doable.
[01:25] Sana: Timeline wise we want to have signals within three weeks, ideally show to execs in five weeks.
[01:31] Javier: Ok target 3-week bench run then a 2-week review, that fits.
[01:35] Priya: On models, quick caveat — open models have tradeoffs. We'll propose a shortlist covering different lat/quality points: a heavier Llama-3 family variant (or Llama-2 70B equivalent if you prefer due to availability), Mistral-instruct type, MPT-30B/ MPT-7B depending on memory, and Falcon-40B / Falcon-7B as a faster low-cost candidate. Also include specialised biomedical fine-tuned variants if needed.
[01:58] Anna: Curious — for biomedical terms will a base open model handle domain-specific jargon or do we need fine-tune/prompting?
[02:06] Priya: Short answer: base models will handle common terms but rare clinical synonyms will need either prompt engineering, retrieval augmentation, or light fine-tuning. For your summarization gold set we recommend a small fine-tune (few-shot adaptation) OR a retrieval-augmented prompt where you surface clinical definitions.
[02:22] Mark: For the POC let's avoid full fine-tune unless necessary. Can we measure quality delta with prompting + retrieval first?
[02:28] Priya: Absolutely, the bench plan includes a prompt + retrieval baseline, then a light fine-tune as an optional second step.
[02:34] Javier: On benchmarks, Priya, can you walk through the metrics you'll capture?
[02:38] Priya: Sure. Latency: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end generation with a 1-2 second SLA target for the synchronous summarization endpoint. Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under batching. Cost: tokens per response and projected $/million tokens using Redwood pricing for both hosted and dedicated profiles. Quality: ROUGE / BERTScore for summarization against the gold set, and F1/accuracy for classification. We'll also capture hallucination rate via heuristic checks and some manual review.
[03:10] Sana: For latency are you assuming GPU-backed inference?
[03:14] Priya: Yes, for production-like tests we'll use our GPU inference nodes with optimized kernels. For the POC we can run both quantized CPU variants for cost comparison and GPU for your target latency.
[03:24] Anna: Ok we especially care about p99 < 2.5s for the summarizer in the demo path.
[03:29] Priya: Noted — we'll track that.
[03:31] Javier: Sizing — what volume are you expecting during the POC?
[03:34] Anna: It's low, maybe 5 tps peak, mostly bursty. Our production target is higher but for POC we want realistic spikes.
[03:41] Priya: 5 tps is small, batching will help cost but keep latency low. We'll simulate bursty traffic in the bench. What about sequence lengths?
[03:49] Mark: Summaries average 1.2k tokens input, outputs around 150-300 tokens. Classifier is short, <256 tokens.
[03:57] Priya: That input length will drive memory profile — for models >30B we recommend offloading/kv caching, and quantization profiles to reduce memory. We'll include memory/kv cache notes in the recommendation.
[04:11] Anna: On model shortlist can you be specific? We need names to evaluate.
[04:15] Priya: Sure. We'll propose: Llama-3-70B (or equivalent Llama-2 70B if you prefer), Mistral Large (mixtral-type), MPT-30B-Long for long-context summarization, Falcon-40B-Instruct, and a smaller MPT-7B for fast/cheap baseline. We'll also add a biomedical-tuned Llama variant (community fine-tune) if you want domain priming.
[04:39] Javier: Also include a quantized 8-bit profile for each candidate so you can see cost/latency tradeoff.
[04:45] Anna: For multilingual classifier — do these models handle Spanish and German well or do we need specific multilingual models?
[04:52] Priya: Llama and Mistral variants have decent multilingual coverage for common languages. For German/Spanish they should be fine, but fine-tuning on your labeled 2k set will give the biggest lift. If you need high accuracy in a low-resource language we might add a multilingual specialist model, but for es/de base models usually do ok.
[05:10] Mark: What about hallucination mitigation — retrieval or followed-by-verify?
[05:14] Priya: Retrieval augmentation is the standard approach — we'll test RAG / top-k context injection. For the summarizer, controlled decoding and post-checks (confidence heuristics) help. We'll include a short eval to compute hallucination rate against the gold set.
[05:27] Sana: Can Redwood run the benchmarks in our VPC or do you need test data to leave our network?
[05:33] Javier: We can run inside your VPC using Redwood Private for the POC; setup takes longer but doable. For initial speed we can run a hosted bench with synthetic data to iterate faster, then move to VPC for the final run.
[05:46] Anna: Ok that sounds fine. One thing — audit and logs: we need full request/response logging and role-based access controls for the POC.
[05:54] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level traces, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. We support SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll share SOC2 and our audit docs.
[06:04] Javier: On pricing — for Dedicated/reserved we'd share estimated $/month given your projected token volumes; for POC we'll offer a time-limited bench credit. I'll send a pricing sheet.
[06:13] Anna: Good. For success criteria: 1) Summarization ROUGE-L within X% of human baseline (Anna: target +10% vs current heuristic); 2) Classifier F1 > 0.88 for en/es/de; 3) p99 latency <2.5s on GPU; 4) Integration checklist done (KMS, VPC, SSO).
[06:33] Priya: Can you confirm ROUGE target more precisely?
[06:35] Anna: We'll add concrete numbers in the success doc, but aim is improvement over current baseline by 10% relative.
[06:41] Javier: Great — so immediate next steps: Javier to share model shortlist + perf spreadsheet, Priya to draft bench plan, Anna to share data slice and success doc, Mark to send VPC network constraints. We'll aim to kick off bench week of 2026-03-29.
[06:55] Mark: One more Q on fallbacks — if a heavier model fails due to capacity, can Redwood route to a smaller quantized model?
[07:02] Priya: Yes that's part of smart routing — fallbacks to cheaper variants or region failover are supported. We'll include routing policy examples in the doc.
[07:10] Anna: Any concerns about PII even if de-identified?
[07:13] Javier: We'll treat data as sensitive, use VPC/private deployment and ensure logs are retained per your policy. We'll sign off on any DPA needed.
[07:21] Sana: Sounds good.
[07:22] Javier: Okay let's recap real quick and close. Next steps and owners as discussed, target bench start week of 3/29, deliverables due 3/27-4/01. Thanks everyone.
[07:34] Anna: Thanks folks.
[07:35] Mark: Thanks.
[07:36] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:37] Javier: Bye.
[07:38] *call ends*

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "Redwood Privat" instead of Private, "K V cash" for KV cache) and some interrupted phrases; kept to reflect Fireflies export style.
